text: Ever since my earliest days, I would tell my parents that I longed to be a painter. Not merely one who dabbles in color, but an artist of such refinement that his fingertips alone might stir the hearts of the masses. A man devoted wholly to the pursuit of beauty, with a dignity befitting one who yearns for everlasting peace.

Imagine it… The castle of Neuschwanstein, enthroned upon its mountain, while solemn pines bow in reverence to its majesty. Or the Vienna Opera House, rendered in hues so daringly abstracted from reality, and yet—still faithful, still sincere in its devotion to truth. With my brush, I believed I could breathe life into the void of an empty canvas, and perhaps one day, see my visions hung within the hallowed halls of the Staatliche Museen zu Berlin.

In those days, the newspapers grew heavier with each passing week. Columns once devoted to art, music, and the affairs of cultured society gave way to reports of harsh rethorics, of ultimatums exchanged between nations, of alliances hardening like iron. In the cafés, men spoke in hushed tones of mobilizations and treaties, their voices carrying both pride and unease. I remember the headlines—bold, unrelenting—announcing that the world stood upon the edge of something vast and terrible. And though I was but a painter in spirit, I could not help but feel the weight of history pressing upon my shoulders.

But as the autumn of my youth approached, the world itself was torn asunder. War swept across the land, and the brilliance of my dreams was smothered beneath a pall of gray. Like countless others, I was summoned to the army. The gentle weight of a lacquered brush was torn from my grasp, replaced by the cold, unyielding wood of a rifle. My hands, once trained to caress the canvas, were now commanded to claw through mud, rubble, and the blasted soil of a ruined earth.

I soon understood: the wind would never again kiss my face as it had in youth. The quietude of home was lost to me, replaced by the ceaseless thunder of artillery and the shrill, merciless ringing of death. In time, I became something less than a man—hollow, godless, a creature of obedience. My life no longer belonged to me, nor to art, nor to beauty. It belonged only to the Fatherland, to the will of its leaders, to the endless demands of war.

To serve. To protect. To conquer. These became the terms of my survival, the creed of my existence. A future for my people, bought with the corpses of our enemies. A fleeting rest for my soul, purchased at the cost of countless others. A dream of peace, forever deferred, forever denied.
And so I march onward. A soldier, nothing more. My brush lies silent, my canvas abandoned. What remains is duty—and the faint hope that, in some distant tomorrow, I may yet dream again.

text: Standing on a well constructed podium, the commander stood firm whilst facing the crowd of disciplined soldiers. Despite the cold, destitute air, the soldiers all lined up as a refined unit doing their utmost to keep up an air of dignity. As the gray skies lurk endlessly behind the commander’s head, the soldiers became slightly rowdy with anticipation of the coming battle.

Company Commander: Men of the 1st company, today is the first of September, 1939 where we shall commence our operation and march onto enemy territory. Our objective is to secure the premises on the south and south western front of Warsaw while the other battalions will secure the north.
Company Commander: In truth.
Company Commander: We are likely to see combat even before the command for the invasion of Warsaw.

Company Commander: But stand proud for you all will have the honor of protecting and fighting in the name of the fatherland. Once we return home victorious, we will not just be remembered as mere soldiers but as heroes that have fought valiantly for the righteousness of our own kin.
Company Commander: So men, may you all stand with the pride of our country as you head into battle today.
Company Commander: Hold your heads up high and face our enemies without remorse.
Company Commander: For glory, for god and for the fatherland.
Company Commander: You all are the hope and future of the people of Germany…

text: Following the orders of his superiors, Heinrich and the assigned platoon were put in charge of securing the western route into the city. Although he had already been accustomed to the life of a soldier, the tumultuous path that the commander had set him on was quite peculiar. The seed of doubt began to sprout within the depths of his mind as he questioned the fact that only a singular platoon was sent alongside him but regardless, Heinrich followed his orders as per usual.

With the Zugführer three in front of him, leading as the head of the line, only the sound of damp boots was audible as his platoon made its way across the forest of slender trees. The temperature was somewhat frigid and the weight of his rifle was unusually heavy but not enough to tamper with his current pacing.
Suddenly, the platoon came to a halt and the Zugführer hunched himself downwards behind a tree.

options.text: Try to figure out the situation first
Follow the leader without question

text: Heinrich falters and momentarily looks around trying to locate the source of the Zugführer’s concern. Before he was able to come to any sort of conclusion, a bullet tore through his head alongside a few of his fellow squad members. His vision turns to black and death embraces him coldly.
[You died]

Almost immediately, six of the platoon’s members were shot down however, Heinrich managed to hide behind the same tree before he was targeted. With around three fourths of the platoon left scattered across the area, a few more who were not well hidden were also shot down.
Agh!?!
Scheisse! My shoulder, my shoulder.
I have been shot, bad.
Zugführer: Men, lay low and stay quiet!
The Zugführer turns his attention to the wounded soldier by his side.
Zugführer: Quiet down Wilhelm, you need to stay calm. That is a non lethal wound, we’ll get a medic to take care of you once we get back from our mission.

Despite his warnings, a swift bullet whizzes through the air and strikes a fatal blow on the panicked soldier leaving his corpse to fall dramatically onto the damp soil below. A few of the soldiers winced in fear and revolt while they themselves inch further away from their fallen comrade. However, unlike those soldiers, Heinrich remains unfazed by sight before him and turns his attention towards the Zugführer.
Heinrich: Zugführer, we have to do something.

options.text: We should stand our ground and return fire.
We should keep moving forward and reposition ourselves.

text: Zugführer: I know I know.
He takes a moment to clear his throat.
Zugführer: Men, return fire!

As the entire platoon returns fire, Heinrich notices that they were heavily outnumbered. Although the initial wave of the enemy fell over, the members of the platoon began to die one by one until there were only five left. Tensely concentrated on the battle, Heinrich momentarily considers his options. Heinrich
Zugführer: I know I know.

options.text: Continue firing
Take cover

text: In the process of returning fire, a bullet pierces through Heinrich’s head completely obliterating his left eye. The rifle falls to the damp soil below as more bullets desecrate Heinrich’s bloodied body. The whole platoon soon meets a similar fate and their bodies and the forest that day had more nutrients to absorb than usual.
[You died]

The remaining members of Heinrich’s platoons were shot dead leaving him all alone hiding behind a tree. Soldiers cautiously enter the now silent forest and check on the dead bodies of his fallen comrades. Heinrich, now left all alone, considers his options once more.

options.text: I surrender!
Stay quiet and pretend to be dead

text: Standing up fervently whilst keeping his arms raised, Heinrich dropped his rifle down and started walking towards the Polish army. Not understanding what Heinrich had just spoken, the Polish soldiers immediately shot him down on the spot. Heinrich succumbs to his wounds and death greets him with its gentle embrace.
[You died]

Heinrich laid his entire body down against the damp soil in an uncomfortable position while the enemy marched on in towards his direction. Soon, a soldier was standing directly in front of him then another passed by. They began to converse in a language foreign to Heinrich and he began to consider his options once more.

options.text: Continue to pretending
Shoot the soldiers before him

text: Out of the corner of his eye, one of the soldiers notices something amiss and decides to check on Heinrich who was laying on his back. Making direct eye contact, Heinrich did his best to remain absolutely still but despite his efforts, a singular drop of sweat traveled from his forehead all the way down to the tip of his nose. Before the Polish soldier could react, sudden artillery fire bombarded the entire area, filling it up in a cloud of dark smog. Unfortunately, Heinrich was directly hit by one of the shells completely decimating his body into tiny particles of flesh.
[You died]

Heinrich manages to shoot one of the soldiers with his rifle before the other topples over him. Wrestling over the weapon in his hand, Heinrich tastes a mixture of dirt and sweat as his head was consecutively bashed against the ground behind. After moments of struggle, Heinrich’s body fails him and the rifle slips away from his grasp. The enemy soldier aimed directly at Heinrich and with a resigning smirk, he violently passed on.
[You died]
Zugführer: I know I know
He takes a moment to clear his throat.
Zugführer: Men, follow me, we are getting out of here!

As the Zugführer started sprinting off towards the opposing end of the forest, Heinrich and the remainder of the platoon bravely followed him through the barrage of gunfire. Their line was slowly trimmed down as the Germans made their way through the dense forest while their pursuers chased them on with caution. The chase carried on with the platoon weaving in and out of occasional thickets while some returned fire. Around 2 kilometers away, from where they originally were ambushed, the sound of artillery crashing down shakes the ground as the screaming of the soldiers begins to escalate. The entire forest violently fell into darkness as waves of artillery shells erupted the latent soil beneath its weight. Regardless, the Zugführer kept on running leaving behind the injured soldiers who were hit by the bombardment and soon, many succumbed to their wounds. However, Heinrich, who was knocked off his feet by a stray artillery, lays on the ground momentarily before another artillery shell strikes a nearby tree. As the dust began to settle, pain roused him to his senses and he looked down to see his thigh had been pierced by a sizable splinter.

options.text: Heinrich: I need to treat my wound.
Heinrich: I need to catch up to the Zugführer.

text: Pulling out the splinter, Heinrich grits his teeth tightly shut together. Blood begins to spill as he tosses the splinter aside and examines the wound carefully. Heinrich sighs in relief as it seems that the wound was not particularly deep but regardless, he began bandaging it up with a spare piece of cloth he always carried with him. As he finished caring for his wound, he looked around and saw that the Zugführer was nowhere to be seen. Suddenly, a small group of Polish soldiers emerge from the depths of the forest. About half of them were battered and wounded by the artillery’s vicious barrage. Heinrich grips his rifle tightly as it occurred to him that he would not be able to run.

options.text: Toss the firearm to the ground and surrender
Try to kill all the enemy soldiers

text: The rifle stiffly falls onto the dirt below as Heinrich raises his hands up and unsteadily gets on his feet. The Polish soldiers momentarily hesitate, unsure about the situation at hand, before pulling out their own weapons and firing them at Heinrich. He promptly dies from multiple bullet wounds to his torso and all was quiet once more in the forest west of Warsaw.
[You died]

Sturdily, the rifle was readily raised and aimed at the group of enemy soldiers before any of them realized what was going on. Two dropped dead almost immediately before the troops backed away looking for cover on the dirt filled battleground. Heinrich was temporarily given a moment to catch his breath.
[You died]

options.text: Continue firing at the enemies
Run for cover

text: As Heinrich continued to suppress the remaining enemies with the loud blaring of his rifle, a sudden bullet jammed his gun. Quickly scraping the bullet away from the barrel way, he swiftly pulled the bolt of his gun and began to re-aim his firearm in the direction of his adversary. However, much to his chagrin, the Polish soldiers had already trained their sites on him and his head was obliterated by the barrage of enemy bullets.

Suddenly stopping his frenzied barrage, Heinrich tries to sprint across the forest but rips over his injured leg. With his face roughly planted into the cold soil, he pushes himself up to his knees panting tiringly before being shot at behind his back. A bullet embeds itself onto his back and he lays down back onto the damp Earth.

options.text: Stay absolutely still
Start crying

text: Heinrich grits his teeth and pretends to be dead. He was determined to make it out alive no matter what battered state his body would be in. However, the Polish soldiers who came to check on him were doubtful of their handiwork. Thus, with a knife of his own, he stabs Heinrich several times, promptly ending the German soldier’s life.
[You died]

Tears flood Heinrich's eyes as sinking emotions heavily inflicts him with a disheartening ailment. He saw only the blackness of dirt and in no way shape or form did he make another attempt of escape. All alone and stranded in enemy territory, he was left for dead several hundred kilometers from home. Heinrich despairing died bleeding out during the invasion of Warsaw, miserable and despondent.
[You died]

Following the Zugführer with a splinter still stuck in his thigh, Heinrich struggles to make his way over a hill. Miraculously, he managed to get over it without further injury and continued following the path the Zugführer took. He finally caught up after a long distance of limping and the Zugführer immediately took notice of him. Spotting the injured soldier limping towards him, the Zugführer helped Heinrich into a small cave before situating himself and tending to Heinrich’s wound. Gregariously positioning Heinrich against the wall, the Zugführer gently pulls out the splinter and bandages Heinrich’s thigh with a piece of cloth. Heinrich winces in pain at the completion of the procedure but soon exhaustingly rests himself, a distance away from the battlefield.
Heinrich: It hurts.

Zugführer: I’m sure it does. But, seeing as you were not bleeding too much, your wound would heal well. If you are lucky, it might not even leave a scar although I would suggest you check in with a proper medic once we get back to base.
Heinrich: That is good to hear.

Heinrich gives out a wry grin to the leader who was distracted, pensively staring out of the cave. Clearly, he was worried about the state of the events that had just occurred and his eyes gave out a sense of dreaded hopefulness.

options.text: Heinrich: Do you think the others would make it here?
Heinrich: Do you think the battle will end soon?
Heinrich: Do you think we would make it out alive?
Heinrich: What should we do now?

text: You died.
[Mission1 fail]
Zugführer: We wait, there is nothing more that we can do.
Heinrich: What about our mission?
Zugführer: Our mission…
He sighs deeply
Zugführer: I had a feeling that it was meant to fail.
Rather,

Our mission was never to secure the western route into the city, but to act as bait to locate the Polish armies. That would explain why those artillery were fired from the direction of our base and why they only sent our platoon this way.

options.text: Heinrich: We were set up for failure?
Heinrich: We were set up to die?

text: Zugführer: That seems to be the case.

He nods solemnly, still staring deep into the forest as dark clouds escape towards the endless sky in the distance. His expression remains silent without any hint of tedium and his eyes seem determined regardless of what reality may suggest otherwise.

Zugführer: Let’s hope that our other men can make it to use and that we do not encounter any more enemies. I don’t believe that the enemy soldiers would pursue us any further given the circumstances that they have to deal with. We shall leave once the battle clears up so for now, we must rest.
With that resolution proposed, the Zugführer turns back to Heinrich.
Zugführer: I dropped my baggage earlier when we were escaping, do you happen to have any water you could share. If you have food, it would be nice if you can give me something to eat as well.

options.text: Give him a snack bar from your pocket
Give him your canteen of water
Give him both
Heinrich: I have nothing to offer you.

text: Zugführer: Thanks

Intently consuming the goods, Heinrich stares at the Zugführer helplessly but he is soon confided by the gentle touch of slumber. Throughout the hours that Heinrich had rested, the Zugführer kept watch at the entrance but no conflict arrived at the hideout nor any of their other men made it to the cave. As the sound of battle began to appease in the distant field, two soldiers suddenly emerged from the dense forest and approached the cave hurriedly. Immediately, the Zugführer woke up Heinrich and they both stared at the dirtied uniforms of the soldier unsure whether it was their allies or enemies. Regardless, the two parties maintained their diplomacy until they were both close enough to ascertain each other's faces and with a grim realization, the Zugführer fired at one of the soldiers. That soldier fell onto one knee and the other enemy soldier deployed a grenade tossing it in the direction of the cave before a second shot finished off the first. Alerted, the Zugführer heads inwards the cave but was blown apart by the grenade while Heinrich was unharmed due to the Zugführer’s body covering much of the explosion. Blood and bits of guts hang loosely from the Zugführer’s torso as Heinrich watches in silent horror seeing the man who was happily eating hours ago torn apart. Drenched in dirt and filth, Heinrich deems it risky to leave the cave thus he lays motionlessly as the second polish soldier closes in on him. Fortuitously, a group of German soldiers closed in on his position and fired at the remaining enemy only to retaliate with another grenade. However, this time, no one was injured and the polish soldier managed to get away from the conflict. Half the allies gave chase while the other went to investigate the cave only to find an injured Heinrich lying helplessly by the floor next to the tattered corpse. Unusually so, Heinrich notices that one of the soldiers in the group was wearing a darker uniform and seemed to be in command of this particular platoon. Regardless, he soon finds himself carried away from the desolate battlefield by the soldiers and soon returned to Germany as the only survivor from his platoon during the siege on west Warsaw.
[Mission1 complete]
Zugführer: Well that is disappointing. I certainly hope you are not withholding any resources for me, we both need to survive after all.
Heinrich: I assure you I am not.
Zugführer: Hmm…

As the Zugführer’s scrutinizing eyes lay upon his wounded body, a sensation of guilt builds itself up from Heinrich’s stomach. Heinrich began reconsidering the decision he had just made and realized that perhaps, it was selfish of him to keep his supplies to himself. Then again, he thought to himself, they had only just met recently and there really was no particular incentive to share his supply to the

text: Heinrich: I really have nothing
Zugführer: I see
He candidly nods.
Zugführer: You are lying aren’t you?
Heinrich: I..
Zugführer: It’s quite alright, rest now Heinrich. I shall go out and find some sustenance for myself.

The Zugführer exits the cave leaving Heinrich staring at the empty space all by himself. Fatigue began to hit him hard and slumber soon encapsulated his consciousness leaving Heinrich vulnerable. Despite that, nothing occurred in the first hour of his sleep but soon the Zugführer arrived back empty handed and fearing for his life. A dark thought occurs within his mind and after careful consideration, the Zugführer, out of desperation, takes Heinrich’s supplies. Waking up by the sudden movements, the Zugführer became flabbergasted with the canteen in one hand and the snack bar in the other. Perplexingly so, the Zugführer immediately puts the items down and lunges at Heinrich. The scuffle was fierce but short lived as the Zugführer choked Heinrich until his wrangling body turned completely limp. Such treason was not tolerated within the battlefield of war otherwise shame would be the last thing a soldier experiences.
[Mission1 complete]
